scope: Second independent targeted manual source pass plus CPU-only index-coverage arithmetic; no learner import/execution, new GPU jobs, source edits or public mutations. Does not infer accuracy from static inspection.

guard.data: Current teacher scores, current student query predictions, and current labelled-train error only.
guard.logic: p*10+t indexes a fresh 10x10 student/teacher confusion table; c[::11]=0 removes agreement. Max off-diagonal confident-count>60 or train mistakes>40 triggers confident teacher-label selection. This is equivariant to any class permutation: the table rows and columns permute together, its diagonal and maximum remain invariant.
guard.work: teacher and every student update, query prediction and training prediction complete before torch.where. No data-dependent Python branch skips fitting or replay. No class ID, dataset identity, query truth, timer or parent state shortcut.
guard.bounds: Student and teacher argmax labels are0..9, so flattened confusion indexes are0..99.

per_call_reset.teacher: Every cloned static input overwritten before replay; captured sym_scores starts with identity transform/zero PCG solutions, computes both current AGOP updates and fresh confident-query pseudo-label refit. Cloned score/metric outputs passed onward.
per_call_reset.student_inputs: Current x, one-hot train y, full train/query pool, teacher targets, same-class training tangents and least-confident query IDs overwrite every persistent data buffer before reset.
per_call_reset.parameters: All encoder/decoder/combinator parameters, beta, gamma initialized each call; all Adam exp_avg/exp_avg_sq/step tensors zeroed. No AMSGrad state exists in configured Adam.
per_call_reset.sampler: Counter resets0; loss-sampling scores reset1; all600 minibatch rows rebuilt from current hard IDs, and RNG reset. LR schedule, mix schedule and row offsets are immutable scalar/index schedules; LR value overwritten at each fwd before opt.step.
per_call_reset.bounds: 20 replays times30 captured updates reads schedule/sampler indexes0..599 then increments counter600, which is reset before next call. Label sampler clamps indices to n-1. Late duplicated query IDs stay inside current pool.
per_call_reset.inference: BN statistics are recomputed from the current supplied training rows during both prediction passes. No persisted running BN stats.

graph_ownership.teacher: CACHE[key]=(g,static,out) strongly retains all external static inputs, outputs and graph. Capture-created intermediate allocations remain in its private pool; side-stream work branches from and rejoins capture stream. Output clone separates later use from teacher scratch.
graph_ownership.student: CACHE strongly retains Ladder, which retains params, all pre-capture input/state/sampler tensors, Adam state and graph. Compiled bound methods also remain on Ladder. No reliance on garbage-collection freeze or hidden compiler cache.
graph_ownership.multi_step: Each of30 captured updates sets every p.grad=None before backward. Gradient and backward workspace created during capture use the graph-private pool; captured kernels refill their static allocations on every replay. Graph is retained for20 ordered replays, and default distinct pools keep teacher/student graph storage separate.
reference_sections: Whole-network capture (grad=None and static gradient refill)

custom_backward_bounds.configured_shapes: M=1,B=2500,S in1024/512/256; custom CombFn is used only for these three wide combinators. Other widths use ordinary combine. Flattened parameter shape has17*S elements; per-column mean/rstd hasS.
custom_backward_bounds.columns: Each supported S divides BC exactly and NCB=S//BC; all unmasked metadata/workspace column accesses therefore remain0..S-1. Unsupported widths fail KCFG lookup rather than silently using mismatched geometry.
custom_backward_bounds.rows: PHASE1/2 use disjoint row chunks with rows<r1 masks, including prefetched rows. Invalid-row GO is zero; partial-gradient contributions are zero, and normalized-v statistic explicitly masks row tails.
custom_backward_bounds.workspace: PHASE1 writes every20*S workspace entry per row chunk, DV and DLAT for every valid row/column. PHASE2 reduces only initialized workspace, with DP e<e_hi<=17*S and WS stride20*S. DP chunks partition17*S; DU writes cover every valid input row/column. Two phases launch in order on current stream.
custom_backward_bounds.gradients: New du/dlat/dp/workspace allocations belong to this op, mutates_args is empty, no caller-input stores. Algebra implements both leaky-ReLU combinator layers plus BN adjoint; BF16 rounding is an ordinary numerical approximation, not a pointer/lifetime issue.
custom_backward_bounds.limitations: Analytical bounds apply to fixed submitted M=1 and configured widths; this pass is not a GPU sanitizer or full floating-point gradient comparison.

conclusion: No confirmed blocker in requested guard, reset, graph-ownership or custom-backward bounds areas. Runtime accuracy/time/energy qualification belongs to the single initial canonical group handled separately.
